claim_one_line: THE FIRST PROOF OF I = 0 IN THE RECORD, ON A NARROW STATED DOMAIN, AND IT USES NONE OF THE THREE MECHANISMS THIS BENCH PROPOSED AND KILLED. Let S = Hom(H_1(M)/<peripheral>, C*) be the cusp-trivial characters and S^0 its identity component, a torus of dimension rank(H_1(M)/<peripheral>). THEOREM: for every chi in S^0, I(W (x) chi) = 0, whenever W restricts to dM self-dually (Sym^m of an SL2 holonomy qualifies). PROOF in six steps: (1) chi cusp-trivial makes (W (x) chi)|_dM = W for every chi, so the cusp matrices never move and t_0, t_0*, t_1 are CONSTANT on S, with t_0 = t_1/2 from t_1 = t_0 + t_0*; (2) r_1(chi) = rank(R(chi)+Bt) - rank(Bt) with Bt constant by (1) and R(chi) Laurent-polynomial in the torus coordinate, so r_1 is lower semicontinuous and attains its MAXIMUM rho on a Zariski-open dense U; (3) r_1(chi) + r_1(chi^-1) = t_1 identically, by Poincare-Lefschetz on (M,dM); (4) inversion is an automorphism of the torus S^0 and S^0 is IRREDUCIBLE, so U and iota(U) are both dense and MEET; (5) at chi in U n iota(U) both r_1(chi) and r_1(chi^-1) equal rho, so 2 rho = t_1 and rho = t_1/2; (6) then for EVERY chi, r_1(chi) <= t_1/2 and r_1(chi^-1) <= t_1/2 while summing to t_1, so both equal t_1/2 -- hence I = t_0 - r_1 = 0. The proof uses NO Galois (ruled out by chirality, B1331), NO cusp-locality (ruled out, B1332 addendum), and NO isotropy (ruled out as the general mechanism, failing in 36 of 40 multi-cusp sectors, B1333 addendum 2): it needs only an identity SYMMETRIC UNDER INVERSION and a family IRREDUCIBLE enough for genericity to bite, which is exactly why it survives chirality, non-isotropy and L_V != L_V* -- only the dimensions ever enter. Cusp-triviality is where step (1) does its work, holding t_1 still while chi moves. SCOPE: non-vacuous exactly when dim S^0 > 0. Of m004's 54 chiral multi-cusped covers to degree ten, dim S = 0 for 52 and dim S = 1 for exactly TWO, d10_4 and d10_35, both 3-cusped with b_1 = 4; on both, the cusp-trivial order-3 characters are EXACTLY the cube-root-of-unity points of S^0, so the theorem covers every twist the programme uses on them and I = 0 there is proved rather than observed. Confirmed numerically at all 36 points of F_37^* on both covers and both germs: t_1 constant, r_1 constant, r_1 = t_1/2, four identities intact, zero skips. WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE, plainly: dim S = 0 for 52 of 54 covers and for EVERY one-cusped manifold including m004 itself and B1330's targets s958, t12833 and t12835, because there b_1(M) equals the peripheral rank and S is FINITE -- a finite set has no Zariski-dense proper open subset, so steps (2), (4) and (5) have nothing to stand on and the vanishing there remains observed and unproved. The open problem is now sharper: find a substitute for Zariski density when S is finite, inversion still being available as a symmetry of the identity but having no connected family to act on. ADDENDUM -- THE MAP OF WHAT IS LEFT, AND A NO-GO. Since dim S = b_1(M) - c by half-lives-in-half-dies, the proof applies exactly when b_1 > c, which a ONE-CUSPED manifold can meet by having b_1 >= 2 -- the method is not intrinsically multi-cusped. But every cover of m004 to degree ten was censused and ALL 23 one-cusped ones have b_1 = 1. NO-GO: peripheral holonomy is unipotent, so Sym^m of it has every eigenvalue 1 and twisting by chi makes every eigenvalue chi(mu); an invariant vector needs eigenvalue 1, so t_0 > 0 iff chi is cusp-trivial, and by T5 the index is IDENTICALLY ZERO off the cusp-trivial locus (the prediction B1333 tested with zero violations in 38070 sectors). Hence on a one-cusped manifold the entire content of the index sits at finitely many RIGID characters, and no character deformation can ever reach it -- not for want of the right family but because the locus carrying the content is zero-dimensional. Deforming rho instead fails too: off the parabolic locus the peripheral holonomy is loxodromic, t_0 drops to 0 and T5 makes the index vanish trivially, so the parabolic point is exactly the rigid one and it is where all the content is. THE MAP: of the 14 chiral multi-cusped covers surveyed exactly, 2 are PROVED by deformation (d10_4, d10_35), 1 is reduced by isotropy (d8_7), and 11 are covered by NEITHER route. The two routes are independent and neither subsumes the other -- on the two covers where deformation works ISOTROPY FAILS (0 of 2), so this is not a dressed-up isotropy argument, while at every one-cusped manifold isotropy holds and deformation fails. So the open problem splits: the ONE-CUSPED case, which is the one the programme needs, has its deformation direction permanently closed by the no-go and reduces entirely to B1332's form-free statement that L_V u L_V = 0 in the SL2-visible part of H^2(T;W (x) W) -- now known to be its ONLY live route; and the several-cusped case with dim S = 0 and isotropy failing, 11 of 14 surveyed, where neither route applies and no third is in hand.
